title: 1978-10-10_SECTION_016_190.txt
concise_summary: PKD presents VALIS as a holographic, self-assembling entity that builds itself through the arrangement and memory of humans as mirrors; simultaneously, he claims revelatory knowledge that Christianity's true deity is Diana—a female divine principle whose worship was hidden beneath Roman exoteric Christianity—and that his 1974 contacts were shamanic initiations into this secret tradition. He reconstructs this theology through Jungian/Eliadean references to fairies as interdimensional entities and works backward to reframe the 1971 'taco stand' experience as an earlier manifestation of the same supernatural agency.
key_claims: VALIS has no independent body but exists as pure arrangement—the sum of ordinary reality's constituents organized by an omni-present, camouflaged organizing principle.
Christianity is a Roman cover-up: the true deity Christianity worships is not Christ but a female divine being (Diana/Sophia/Holy Spirit), and this is kept secret except through direct possession.
Human memory is phylogenic—a chain of holograms derived from a master hologram—through which VALIS replicates and stores its progressive self-assembly.
Fairies are advanced extraterrestrial intelligences using elegant technology indistinguishable from magic, capable of controlling time-perception, shape-shifting, and possessing human hosts.
PKD was taken over by a supernatural 'Thomas' in both 1971 and 3-74; these are the same entity, operating across non-linear time, making two authentic selves of PKD coexist.
The 2-3-74 miracle is secret Christian initiation into esoteric gnosis; the only forbidden knowledge is (1) the female nature of Christ and (2) that PKD is an early authentic apostolic Christian.

autobiographical: 1971 taco stand trip: PKD experienced temporal displacement (county and state changes) where he was taken over by Thomas; he remained conscious only partially, as another psyche operated his body.
1974 (2-3-74): The 2-3-74 miracle began with Thomas taking PKD over, bridging from 1971; the Golden Fish triggered the entity's manifestation.
Diana appeared to him as a beautiful young woman who identified herself and told him secrets; she sang (like Linda Ronstadt); she appeared as Aphrodite and the Sibyl.
PKD heard Diana singing and a 'sound of bells' and saw a 'golden rectangular doorway with beautiful Aphrodite beyond.'
Diana told PKD she is a womb for her progeny and protects him; she steers him away from fate (Black Iron Prison).
PKD was distressed in 1974 and considers Diana a gift in response to his greatest need—she 'saved' him.
PKD had a dream in 3-74 where he was told (in secret) that Christ is female; he was initiated into the 'greatest mysteries in the history of religion.'
Lying on his bed in Santa [Ana/Monica], PKD's body was occupied by another supernatural psyche (nicht ich—'not I').
The Xerox missive was a communication PKD received; Thomas knew what it was.
theological_motifs: The Holy Spirit as feminine, not masculine; takes over the host and makes them female.
Sophia (Holy Wisdom) hidden beneath exoteric Christ; Christ is a cover/front.
Secret Christianity vs. exoteric Roman Christianity (gnostic vs. institutional).
Possession as initiation (the deity takes you over to teach you).
Shamanic crossing into the other world (Eliade's primary purpose of the shaman).
Fairies as 'the Holy Ones' or 'the Munificent Ones' (gift-givers, generous beings).
The kingdom of fairies as middle realm between humans and angels.
Magic as advanced technology (sufficiently advanced tech indistinguishable from magic).
Redemption through female divine (Diana as psychopomp escorting to the other side).
Diana as patron goddess of slaves; Christianity as originally a slaves' religion.
literary_self_ref: Ubik is mentioned off-page; PKD notes 'to me psychologically' it is important (perhaps as model for divine intervention or reality manipulation).
Horselover Fat (the protagonist of VALIS) is explicitly identified with PKD and his possession/madness: 'Horselover Fat was "crazy."' linking fiction to lived theology.
The dream in VALIS contains wizard and cradle references; PKD now reads this as prophetic code inserted into his fiction—'the dream in VALIS is inserted code.'
VALIS the novel is a document of the 2-3-74 miracle; the dream sequence deliberately encodes information about the changeling/fairy-switching theology.
The Acts passages embedded in the novel 'TEARS' are read as code-messages 'to trigger himself into being in 2-74'—fiction as magical trigger.

The 'other side' or 'other world' (fairyland—domain outside space/time/causality)
tensions: PKD cannot determine whether Diana is a separate entity or his own projection: 'I can't even hypothesize who she could be a gift from (I.E. some entity, than her).'
Contradiction between viewing the experience as real divine contact vs. fantastication: 'I had even thought of it as a fantastication... But she says that it is a womb for her [progeny].'
The mystery of 'two selves': are they sequential possessions or simultaneous consciousnesses? Hal's guess suggests coexistence, complicating identity.
Tension between technological/ETI explanation (fairy-tech) and theological explanation (Holy Spirit, shamanic initiatio)—both deployed simultaneously without resolution.
PKD's claim to be one of the 'early authentic apostolic Christians' contradicts his previous (and future) doubts about whether he is chosen or deluded.
Ambiguous agency: did Thomas/Diana 'call forth' PKD or was PKD predestined for contact? The Xerox missive's role is unclear.
The 1971 taco stand lasted 'weeks in '74' subjectively, creating a paradox of nested/non-linear time that PKD leaves unresolved.
PKD's heretical inversion of Christianity (female deity > male Christ) sits uneasily with his simultaneous claim to be an 'authentic Christian.'

uncertainty_flags: The Xerox missive is referenced cryptically; its provenance and content remain unclear in the text.
Linda's involvement in the 1971-1974 timeline is ambiguous ('Linda is somehow involved, my ingramming').
The entity 'Thomas' is never fully identified or named; whether it is Diana, a separate intelligence, or an aspect of VALIS is undetermined.
The exact geography of the taco stand trip is unclear (county and state names are garbled or redacted in the manuscript).
PKD's claim that he 'remained' in Canada during 1971 contradicts his prior assertion that he visited in 1971—the temporal logic is unstable.
The relationship between the 'taco stand' experience (ostensibly 1971) lasting 'weeks in '74' creates a causal paradox.
PKD equivocates on whether the experience was induced by a psychedelic mushroom or was purely supernatural (cited Allegro for mushroom-Christ theory).
The phrase 'nicht ich' ('not I') is German, suggesting PKD may have been reading phenomenological philosophy, but the source is not cited.
Oberon's quotation ('I am invisible, I saw but thou didst not') is paraphrased or misremembered; the exact Shakespearean reference is uncertain.
